value.name: Asha packs for departure
value.description: Asha organizes her bag methodically, preparing for her trip while Rosa's message remains unanswered.
evidence: Asha closed the laptop and went back to the bag on the kitchen chair, working through it the way she worked through an exhibit list: toiletries zipped into the inner pocket, two blouses folded flat, the printed itinerary tucked against the lining where she could find it without looking.

value.name: Asha checks departure against deposition
value.description: She verifies the Thursday departure time against her last deposition slot, showing how tightly scheduled the trip is.
evidence: She checked the Thursday departure time once more against her last deposition slot, then again

value.name: Rosa informs Asha about the fall
value.description: Rosa texts that the nursing staff mentioned his fall and offers help with discharge papers.
evidence: Rosa: The nursing staff mentioned his fall. If you need help navigating the discharge papers, just reach out.

value.name: Asha realizes others know about the fall
value.description: Reading Rosa's text, Asha understands that people in Trenton already know about the fall and the paperwork ahead.
evidence: Asha read it standing, one hand still on the strap of the bag, and the small efficient world she had been building around the trip widened by exactly that much—someone in Trenton already knew about the fall, already knew which forms would be on the table, and was telling her so without asking anything in return.

value.name: Asha leaves the message unanswered
value.description: Asha does not reply to Rosa, but keeps the phone visible beside her packed bag before moving on.
evidence: She did not answer, but she did not turn the phone over either; she left it face up beside the packed bag and went to find her shoes.

value.name: Asha drafts a question about the fall
value.description: Before putting on her shoes, Asha picks up the phone again and asks what the staff said about the fall.
evidence: Asha picked the phone back up before she had her shoes on, the strap of the bag still slung over the chair behind her, and thumbed out the question she had been avoiding by not answering: What did the staff say about the fall.
